biography.plain_text: Richard Burton was a Welsh actor whose career spanned Shakespeare, musical theatre and Hollywood. His commanding voice and performances in Becket and Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? brought international recognition and seven Academy Award nominations. He also played King Arthur in Camelot, moving between the demands of stage performance and cinema.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before becoming Richard Burton, Richard Jenkins left school to help support his family when his brother-in-law could no longer work. A former teacher arranged his return, bringing him under the influence of Philip Burton. The English teacher coached his speech and took him onto Margam Mountain to practise projecting his voice. When Philip became his legal guardian, Richard adopted his surname.

That training helped shape a career built around language. After a short RAF course at Oxford and military service, Burton returned to professional acting. His reading as First Voice in the BBC’s original Under Milk Wood brought Dylan Thomas’s imagined Welsh community to radio audiences. He recorded it after attending only the final rehearsal.
